concepts.title: Fractals and Self-Similarity
concepts.definition: A fractal is a shape built by repeating the same pattern at smaller and smaller scales, so parts look like copies of the whole - fern leaves, tree limbs, coastlines, clouds, temple tiers at Khajuraho and Escher's lizard prints all carry this self-similar structure.
concepts.key_idea: Same rule, applied forever: every piece mirrors the whole at a smaller scale.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp204.txt lines 5-30 (fractals in nature), 100-150 (fractals in art)

solution_steps.explain: Find the copy of the whole shape that appears inside itself.
Each new generation must reproduce the pattern at a smaller scale.
Ferns, trees, temple tiers and Escher prints follow exactly this repetition.

concepts.title: Sierpinski Carpet Counts
concepts.definition: The Sierpinski Carpet starts from a square cut into 9 with the centre removed; every surviving square spawns 8 squares at the next step, so the count of remaining squares at step n is 8 to the power n, while holes accumulate as 1 + 8 + 64 + ... after each step.
concepts.key_idea: Each survivor makes 8 children: R0 = 1, R1 = 8, R2 = 64.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp204.txt lines 30-70 (Sierpinski carpet, Rn = 8n, Hn recurrence)
question_patterns: how many squares remain at step 2 of the Sierpinski carpet

how does the recurrence R(n+1) = 8 Rn lead to 8 to the power n

solution_steps.explain: Each step multiplies the surviving squares by 8.
Every survivor of the previous step leaves one new hole, so holes add the previous survivors.

concepts.title: Sierpinski Triangle Counts
concepts.definition: Joining midpoints of an equilateral triangle makes 4 identical triangles and removing the centre one leaves 3; each survivor repeats this, so the number of shaded triangles at step n is 3 to the power n, and holes build up as 1 + 3 + 9 + ...
concepts.key_idea: One triangle becomes 3 survivors: 1, 3, 9, 27 at successive steps.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp204.txt lines 70-100 (Sierpinski gasket and its figure it out)

solution_steps.explain: Each previous survivor leaves one hole in the next step.

concepts.title: Koch Snowflake Sides and Perimeter
concepts.definition: In the Koch snowflake every side splits into 3 and the middle third becomes a bump of two new sides, so each step quadruples the side count and thirds the side length; starting from 3 unit sides, step n has 3 x 4 to the n sides and perimeter 3 x (4/3) to the n.
concepts.key_idea: Sides multiply by 4, length divides by 3, so the perimeter keeps growing by 4/3 each step.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp204.txt lines 100-135 (Koch snowflake construction and figure it out)
question_patterns: how many sides does the Koch snowflake have at step 2
find the perimeter at step 1 when the starting triangle has sidelength 1

describe how the bump replaces the middle third of a side

solution_steps.explain: Each step replaces every side by 4 smaller sides.
Each side shrinks to a third of the previous, so the length is 1 over 3 to the n.
Total perimeter is the side count times one segment length.

concepts.title: Visualising Solids Through Profiles
concepts.definition: Seeing a solid really means seeing its outline, or profile, from one viewpoint; the same cylinder can show a rectangle from the side and a circle from above, and imagination drills like cutting a square's corners at edge midpoints reveal hidden shapes such as a smaller square or an octagon.
concepts.key_idea: One solid, many profiles: viewpoint decides whether you see a square, circle or triangle.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp204.txt lines 152-260 (build it in your imagination, profiles 5-12)

concepts.title: Making Solids and Their Nets
concepts.definition: Basic solids like cuboids, cylinders and cones can be built from flat sheets, and reading or drawing their unfoldings connects 2D outlines to 3D objects; hands-on construction confirms which faces glue together and how the flat pattern wraps into the solid.
concepts.key_idea: Flat patterns fold into solids: the net lists every face exactly once.
